Alcohol feedback remained heterogeneous: m205 was underestimated, m206 was overpredicted at 1/1 but close at 5/1, and m119 was close at 1/1 yet underestimated at 5/1. The new alcohol choices therefore emphasize intermediate conditions and fused-versus-ether transfer. The m81 5/1 loading pair showed earlier onset at high loading but no universal completion shift, reinforcing an interaction rather than a single loading correction. m129 at 20/1 was much closer than its 5/1 prediction, so the new 2/1 and 10/1 points target the transition. The 1500-ul cinnamic-acid measurements reduced confidence that the 2000-ul completion maximum should be propagated unchanged, motivating another matched plug-volume ratio point. The m23 acquisition corrected the endpoint-ordering question at 1/1 enough to justify a follow-up curve point rather than treating the original prediction as a label.","batch_rationale":"The batch repairs several observed failure regions while preserving scientifically meaningful local contrasts. Nitrogen rows cover m90 and m88 solvent transitions, m36 and m141 structure-condition transfer, and aminoaryl positional controls. Alcohol rows map the m205 and m119 response curves. Loading rows extend the inconsistent m81 and m25 evidence and add m28 and m107 high-retention loading contrasts. Ratio experiments target the m129 transition, cinnamic-acid plug-volume behavior, and m23 endpoint ordering. The remaining selections sample high-width, low-similarity carbonyl, halogen, aminoaryl, ether, and nitro-alcohol regions so retraining can improve structural transfer rather than only correcting known molecules. The batch avoids redundant identical tuples and combines local response-curve information with broad chemical coverage, which should improve V1/V2 generalization across both repeated condition families and underrepresented structures."}
